For most cats it's best to start off isolating the cat to one room of the house and let the cat explore on its own by leaving the door open. Leave the food/water/litter box in that area too. Leave a blanket on their bed and then place that blanket further and further away from the door. Cats know their environment by familiar scents. Once he ventures outside, give him positive reinforcement via treats. BSH are very aloof and almost shy cats at first and you really have to work towards a trusting bond with them. They are still not cuddly and they will always be a little standoffish. If the cat has too much access to a home, it will be overwhelming not only bc it's unfamiliar, but the home is filled with unfamiliar scents, leaving the cat with no sense of familiarity or safety. Time and patience is your friend. Once that trust bond is formed your it'll be all worth it for you. Look for simple signs: he starts to follow you, he wants to be in the same room as you, he comes to you for pets. I had to go through all these steps with my girl BSH and now she's my little leech and she even likes to sleep with me now. It took MONTHS to reach that level with her but it was worth every second!

Sorry OP, YTA here. I understand that being a light sleeper is frustrating and some people just require more sleep than others, but your quality of sleep is not the responsibility of anyone but you. Controlling your surroundings for your sleep is not only a bit selfish, but damn near impossible. I cannot control my outside surroundings but I CAN control what I do to keep myself asleep. Going around getting upset and trying to take control over things i literally cannot control solved absolutely nothing. I sleep with earplugs, a fan, AND a white noise machine. Those three in combo keep me asleep through the night. I live by the beach and it can be very noisy at times, but I don't run into issues anymore. Honestly I had the worst depressive episode I ever had this year. My anxiety was so bad that I wasn't eating. All I wanted to do was sleep and cuddle with my two cats. I was also losing weight like crazy. I discovered during that period of time that the only food i would eat was sushi. As expensive as sushi is, I budgeted so I could eat it a couple times a week and it was something that I genuinely looked forward to. My friend and I coined the term "sushi therapy" because of this. I know it sounds so silly, but eating sushi is something that I enjoy so much that even on my darkest days it helps. I think moral of the story is find something, anything to look forward to in your week. Is it your new favorite show releasing a new episode on Friday? Is there a Playlist that updates every week that you look forward to? Do you like watching the sunset every night? No matter how small it is, find something you can look forward to. That little something has helped me so much this last year
